title: Modi and Nepal PM Balendra Shah hold talks in Delhi; India 'positive' on $2 billion aid request
dek: Shah received a ceremonial welcome at Rashtrapati Bhavan before delegation-level talks at Hyderabad House. A new air entry route, including a disputed proposal involving Bagdogra, was still unresolved going into the talks.
author: Declaration Desk
body:
Prime Minister Narendra Modi and Nepal's Prime Minister Balendra Shah held delegation-level talks at Hyderabad House in New Delhi on Monday, on the second day of Mr Shah's State visit, his first bilateral trip abroad since taking office in March. Agreements and memorandums of understanding were scheduled to be exchanged after the talks, followed by a joint press statement; the full list of outcomes had not been published at the time of this update.

Earlier on Monday Mr Shah received a ceremonial welcome and guard of honour at Rashtrapati Bhavan, with Mr Modi present, and laid a wreath at Rajghat, according to reports. New Delhi had responded positively to Nepal's request for about $2 billion in grants and lines of credit, according to reports from Kathmandu on Sunday, though the terms had not been announced.

## The air-route dispute

One unresolved issue has a direct Bengal angle. Nepal wants an additional entry route for international flights through Indian airspace, and wants its western L626 route, which aircraft can currently use only to leave Nepal, to work in both directions. The two sides had not agreed going into Monday's talks, according to reports. India proposed that aircraft use the route at 39,000 feet, while Nepal wants about 29,000 feet, one report said.

Reports differ on the Bagdogra element. One report from Kathmandu said India had proposed that its military aircraft be allowed to use an entry point near Bagdogra, the airport serving Siliguri and north Bengal, and quoted a Nepali official as saying: "We have made it clear that we can allow civilian flights, not military ones." Earlier reports had said India offered a route into Nepal's Bhairahawa airport if flights to and from Bagdogra could use Nepal's eastern airspace.

## Sunday's arrival

Mr Shah arrived on Sunday and was received at Indira Gandhi International Airport by Jitin Prasada, Minister of State for Commerce and Industry. External Affairs Minister S. Jaishankar called on him later that day. The Ministry of External Affairs (MEA) said in a post on X that the visit "provides an opportunity to strengthen the enduring and multifaceted partnership between India and Nepal".

Announcing the visit at his bi-weekly briefing on Friday, MEA spokesperson Randhir Jaiswal said Mr Shah, widely known as Balen, would receive full State honours. "This will be a State Visit and first visit to India after assuming office by the honourable Prime Minister of Nepal," he said, calling it "a very important visit for us".

## What is on the table

Mr Jaiswal said the talks would cover development cooperation, people-to-people ties, energy and connectivity, and newer areas such as start-ups, technology, innovation and sport, including cricket, which he said had become "an important connect" between the two countries. Nepal's Foreign Secretary Amrit Bahadur Rai said the two sides expected to inaugurate completed connectivity and energy projects and lay foundation stones for new ones, according to reports. Mr Shah is also due to address a Nepal-India business forum.

Finance Minister Swarnim Wagle and Foreign Minister Shishir Khanal are among a 34-member official delegation, and a separate 52-member business delegation is travelling at its own expense, according to reports. Nepal also wants to use the visit to find ways to raise its exports to India, its largest trading partner, according to reports. The two sides are expected to exchange memorandums of understanding on education, health, agriculture, sport, disaster management and human resource development.

After the Bhotekoshi floods in August, Nepal asked for about $2 billion for reconstruction of roads, bridges and other infrastructure, made up of $1 billion in soft loans, $500 million in grants and $500 million for post-flood rebuilding, according to reports. Indian officials described a "substantive" package as under discussion before the visit, reports said; another report said India could insist on phased, project-by-project disbursement.

## Power, borders and recruitment

Nepal already exports about 1,200 MW of electricity to India, according to reports, and the talks are expected to cover transmission lines, access to India's power market and joint hydropower projects such as Lower Arun and Pancheshwar. The Arun-3 project is being built by the Indian public sector company Satluj Jal Vikas Nigam.

Two sensitive issues are also expected to come up. Nepal claims the Kalapani, Lipulekh and Limpiyadhura areas, which India administers, and lodged a formal protest in May after India and China agreed to resume border trade through the Lipulekh pass, which restarted on 1 August. Recruitment of Nepali Gorkhas into the Indian Army has been suspended since India moved to the Agnipath scheme in 2022, according to reports.

## Why it matters

Nepal borders five Indian states, including West Bengal, and its hydropower and rivers feed into the Ganga system that flows through Bengal. India and China have long competed for influence in Kathmandu: while Mr Shah is in Delhi, a 20-member Nepali parliamentary team is on a 10-day visit to China to discuss stalled infrastructure projects and closed border trading points, according to reports. The MEA describes the visit as part of India's "Neighbourhood First" policy.

Mr Shah, a former mayor of Kathmandu, became prime minister on 27 March after his Rastriya Swatantra Party's election victory. He visited New York in September for the UN General Assembly.

## What happens next

The two leaders were due to flag off the Saryu-Kamala Express, a new weekly rail service of about 604 km between Ayodhya and Janakpur due to begin regular runs on 28 November, and to unveil a joint vision document titled "Samriddha Nepal, Samunnat Bharat", according to reports. Mr Modi was to host a lunch for the delegation. Mr Shah was scheduled to call on President Droupadi Murmu at 3.15 pm and to leave Delhi at 4.50 pm. The Declaration will update this story when the official list of outcomes is released.
